items.title: Community Heritage Fund Program Establishment
notes: Report from M. Iglesias, Manager of Planning Services

M. Iglesias, Manager of Planning Services provided an overview of the report, indicating Heritage grant programs provide financial assistance to property owners to help with the costs associated with conservation efforts, which may include restoring, preserving and rehabilitating heritage properties.
She outlined the details of the program which included:
• Grant available to owners of designated properties, 115 in Centre Wellington,
• Matching grants would be given funding up to 50% of a project, up to $10,000,

• Applications would have to meet generally accepted heritage practices and principles as set out in Canada’s Standards and Guidelines, • Applicants would have to adhere to rules as set out in the by-law and meet specific requirements such as obtaining a heritage permit, • One per year, can be stacked,
• Call for applications would generally open beginning of each year and close end of February (March this year) so applications can be weighed against each other,

• Authority would be delegated to Planning staff to administer the program, but an existing sub-committee of Heritage will review the applications and make recommendations, with support from planning staff,
• Annual available funds will be confirmed through the budget process and staff will report back annually on program uptake.

M. Iglesias indicated staff is requesting Council approval of the program to encourage conservation of the Township’s heritage resources over the long term, which is beneficial to the community, and also to encourage additional designations.
M. Iglesias responded to questions regarding the impact of legislative changes to the inventory of listed properties and the timing of the budget process related to the allocation of the OLG funding.
